risks.risk: Housing seam could indicate the case was previously opened or cracked, affecting seal integrity and internal component condition.
risks.proof: A close-up, well-lit photo of the seam line from multiple angles, or a photo showing intact factory crimp/seal marks.
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly opened/repaired, lowering confidence in internal condition

risks.risk: Brushes, slip rings, and bearings could be worn, causing noise or charging failure not visible in current photos.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of brush length and slip ring surface, plus a short video of the pulley spinning freely by hand.

risks.risk: Electrical output (voltage/current) could be below spec despite visual completeness.
risks.proof: A video of the alternator running on a bench/test rig with a multimeter showing charging voltage (~13.5-14.5V).

risks.risk: Connector pins or regulator could be damaged/corroded, affecting fitment or function.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the electrical connector and regulator unit.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having unverified electrical faults

proof_requests: Clear, in-focus photo of the part number sticker showing the full code '439741' or equivalent Valeo reference.
Short video of the alternator spinning and charging on a bench test rig with a multimeter display visible.
Close-up photos of the housing seam from both sides to confirm it is a factory joint, not a crack or prior repair.
Close-up photo of brushes/slip rings and the electrical connector.
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type and brand (Valeo alternator for Mercedes-Benz M278) even though the specific part number and all performance claims remain unverified, so it can be priced at worst case pending proof of testing and internal condition.
